title: Average Causal Slope Estimation When Conditional Dose Variance Vanishes
banked_reason: D0.5: central feasible minimax and honest-length frontier for psi is not delivered; paper score ceiling 6.4 below field floor 7.4.
gap_reasons: The central feasible minimax and honest-length frontier for psi is not delivered.
The full rate, the possible scale-slope phase when s<eta, and the sharp kappa=1 logarithms remain in oeq:full-frontier, oeq:scale-slope-phase, and oeq:critical-logs.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved an exact no-log risk and honest-length frontier for the globally normalized Psi, an oracle frontier for psi, smooth-quadrant observable attainment, and a same-class rough lower obstruction. D0.5 found that the promised feasible psi frontier for all positive smoothness remains open, including the scale-slope phase and critical kappa=1 logarithms; the delivered package therefore missed the field floor. Three bounded referee fixes to the Psi projection, interval map, and literature positioning remain for any reuse of that partial result.
tldr: The average conditional causal slope \(\psi\) is point identified in the scalar Gaussian continuous-dose benchmark even though treatment variance vanishes like \(x^{\kappa}\). Its oracle frontier is proved, and an observable within-bin estimator and uniformly honest interval attain that frontier when \(s,\eta>1/2\); the full feasible frontier for arbitrary positive \(s,\eta\), the possible scale--slope phase, and the sharp \(\kappa=1\) logarithms remain open. For the globally normalized causal slope \(\Psi\), the projected ratio estimator and interval attain the exact no-log orders \(R_{\Psi,n}\asymp n^{-1}\vee n^{-8\eta/(4\eta+1)}\) and \(L_{\Psi,n}\asymp n^{-1/2}\vee n^{-4\eta/(4\eta+1)}\), with the sole root-n elbow at \(\eta=1/4\).
gap: Theorem 4 of Hines, Diaz-Ordaz, and Vansteelandt excludes vanishing conditional treatment variance, while their Theorem 5 leaves arbitrary rough Holder nuisances outside its rate conditions. Existing conditional-covariance, variance-estimation, and weak-overlap theorems each omit at least one of the singular ratio, exact Gaussian dose law, unknown scale, causal slope, or uniformly honest length criterion.
fill: A matched frontier based on close-pair local covariance and variance recovery, polynomial annihilation, finite Gaussian-moment normalization, and multiscale Gaussian mixtures will characterize feasible risk and honest length rather than infer regularity from a formal influence curve.
